_comment: Phase 8a. The single most important payment-system health signal, per the
phase plan's own words - and the exit criterion left half-built until now:
the poller was measured (experiment 20), the alert was not.
AGE, NOT COUNT - THE SAME LESSON THIS PROJECT KEEPS RELEARNING
payorch.payments.unknown is published too and is deliberately not the
threshold here. A steady hundred UNKNOWN payments that each resolve within
a minute is a busy system behaving correctly; three that have sat for an
hour is a provider that stopped answering, and count cannot tell those
apart. This is phase 4e's HTTP-5xx mistake in a new shape - see
docker/signoz/alerts/03-payment-failure-rate.json - and UnknownResolverMetrics
was written with this alert already in mind: 'the number to alert on' is
its own comment on the gauge below.
THE THRESHOLD IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN
10800s (3h), against a computed worst case of ~2.05h for a SINGLE payment
resolving entirely through normal backoff and never once getting an answer:
base-backoff-ms=60000, max-backoff-ms=3600000, max-attempts=8
plus initial-delay-ms=60000                   = 124min ~ 2.05h
A payment can legitimately sit UNKNOWN for two hours while the poller is
doing exactly its job - working through the doubling backoff toward
UNRESOLVED. A threshold below that fires on the poller working correctly,
which is 04-egress-limiter-saturation.json's trap in reverse: an alert that
cries wolf during a clean run gets muted. 3h clears the worst case with an
hour of margin, so this fires only once the poller SHOULD have already
given up and has not, or has stopped running entirely.
-1 IS HANDLED THE SAME WAY 02-provider-p99-breach.json HANDLES IT
PaymentPersistence.oldestAgeInState returns a real Duration or Duration.ZERO
when the backlog is empty - not a sentinel - so an empty backlog reads as
age 0, which is below the threshold and cannot fire. There is no equivalent
of provider-p99-breach's -1 case here because 'no UNKNOWN payments' is an
unambiguous zero, not a missing measurement.
NO alertOnAbsent, same reasoning as 06-dlq-pending.json
UnknownResolverMetrics only binds when payorch.recon.unknown-poller.enabled
is true (UNKNOWN_POLLER_ENABLED, off by default). Absence-alerting would fire
on every stack that has not turned the poller on, which is most local runs -
and the series that answers 'is the poller alive at all' is a different
question from 'is the backlog aging out', which this rule is about.

annotations.summary: A payment has been UNKNOWN for over 3 hours
annotations.description: The oldest UNKNOWN payment has aged past the poller's own worst-case resolution time (~2h through 8 backoff attempts). Either the poller has stopped resolving it, or it has stopped running. Check GET /actuator/health for the poller and payorch.recon.polled / payorch.recon.inconclusive for whether it is still trying. Every payment in this state may have moved money nobody has confirmed.
